texto: KORbuild is sold as a subscription (SaaS). Each customer is a company with its own account, its own people and its own data. This page explains who the customers are, who registers what, and what each company can see of the others. Read it before the presenter's guide: every screen in the demo follows these rules.

Customer In the US market What it does in KORbuild General contractor (GC) General contractor Manages the jobs. It registers the jobs, links its subcontractors to them and follows everything they do. It does not fill out daily reports or clock anyone in. Subcontractor Trade contractor (concrete, framing, siding, drywall…) Does the work. It keeps the daily report, the crew time clock and the schedule of its own work, measures plans and sends proposals. This guide is for the person who will present KORbuild to a customer. You do not need to know the system beforehand: follow the order below, sign in with the users indicated, and use the "what to say" boxes as your script. A presentation of Daily and Crew takes about 25 minutes; with questions, plan for 40.

Construction companies in the US run their jobs on paper, text messages and spreadsheets. The superintendent writes the daily report at night (or not at all), the office chases people by phone, and when a client disputes a delay there is no reliable record of what happened on site. KORbuild is one platform, one set of jobs and people, with modules the company turns on as it needs them: Module In one sentence Who uses it Daily The daily construction report, filled out on the phone in minutes, approved by the office and shared with the client as a sealed PDF. titulo: Act 1 — One platform, many modules (2 min)
texto: Sign in as Tom Reilly (Admin of Northfield, a sub with every module). Show the modules screen: Daily, Crew, Measure and Settings, each with a short description. The modules screen of a subcontractor with every module Mention that a general contractor sees fewer modules: it manages the jobs, so it has Daily (to follow and approve) and Settings, but no time clock or takeoff of its own. What to say "Each company turns on the modules it needs. The jobs, people and contacts are entered once and used by every module. The subs do the work and record it; the general contractor follows and approves."

Question Answer Does it work without internet? Yes. The app is saved on the phone after the first visit; reports and punches are stored on the phone and upload when there is signal. Do I need to install an app? Not in the prototype: it runs in the browser and can be added to the home screen. App Store and Google Play versions are planned. Can the foreman change a report after approval? No. Approval seals it. Changes are requested before approval ("Request changes from the field"). What does the client need? Nothing: they receive a link and can download the PDF. No account, no cost. Can the gen

Daily is the daily construction report (in Portuguese, RDO). Every workday, the subcontractor's person in charge on site records the weather, the crew, the equipment, the work performed, the issues and the photos. The general contractor of the job reviews and approves the report — or the subcontractor itself, on a job it has directly with the owner — and the approved report is sealed and shared with the client as a link or a PDF. See How KORbuild is organized.

A record that holds up. When a client disputes a delay, the daily reports are the contractor's evidence: rain that stopped the pour, a late delivery, a missing inspection. Photos carry date, time and GPS inside the image, and the approved report is sealed. Reports that actually get done. Each job has a person responsible for its report, a daily deadline (6 PM) and reminders. The office sees the next morning which jobs did not report. Minutes, not an evening. On the phone, the foreman copies yesterday's report, adjusts the crew, dictates what was done and takes the photos. It works without sign

Crew: when a report starts, the crew can be filled in from the people who clocked in on the job that day (Update from the crew that clocked in). This manual walks through Daily one task at a time. The first part is for the field (on the phone); the second, for the office (on the computer). Screen names, buttons and messages are written exactly as they appear in KORbuild, in bold. Before you start Daily opens in the area of your role: the field starts on Today, the office on the Dashboard. On the phone, the menu is at the bottom of the screen; on the computer, on the left. If you do not see a screen described here, your role does not include it — see Roles and permissions.

titulo: Field: see what is due today
texto: What it is for: knowing, at a glance, which reports you owe and which ones the office sent back. Who can do it Anyone who fills out daily reports (default role: Foreman). Open KORbuild and tap Daily on the modules screen. It opens on Today. Read the boxes at the top, from most to least urgent: red — late report: a past workday without a report. Tap the job to fill it out now. yellow — today's report is missing: jobs without today's report, with the deadline and the time left (for example, Due: today at 6 PM · 1h30 left). red — the office requested changes: a report sent back, with the reason i

titulo: Field: fill out the daily report
texto: What it is for: recording the day on the job: weather, crew, equipment, what was done, what got in the way, and photos. Who can do it The person responsible for the job's report, or anyone with Fill out daily reports (default role: Foreman). On Today, tap the job. The job screen shows the date, the deadline and the previous reports. Tap New daily report to start blank, or or copy from a previous report to start from another day (see Copy a previous report). The job screen: start a new report, copy a previous one or log no work today The report opens. At the top, the progress chips (Weather, Cr

The weather is pulled automatically from the job location for the morning (7 AM–12 PM) and the afternoon (1 PM–5 PM). With more than 2 mm of rain in a period, that period is marked Not workable. Check or correct each period: Sunny, Cloudy or Rain, and Workable or Not workable. Get weather automatically fetches it again (it needs signal). The report says whether the weather was automatic, adjusted by hand or entered by hand. Weather, morning and afternoon

Tap the trades (+ Mason, + Laborer, + Carpenter…) to add them, then use − and + to set how many were Present and Absent. A trade that is not in the list: type it in Other trade and tap Add. Update from the crew that clocked in fills the crew from the people who clocked in on this job today in Crew (the time clock). The section shows the total present (for example, 13 present). Crew: present and absent by trade
Add the equipment on site with its quantity and status: Running, Idle or Under maintenance. Equipment on site

Each activity has: Field What to enter Description What was done. Example: poured the 2nd floor slab, 60 cu yd. Location / phase Where on the job (floor, building, area). Status In progress or Completed. Schedule task and % complete Only when the job has a schedule: the task this activity advanced and how far it is now. The schedule is updated when the office approves the report. Dictate: speak instead of typing (uses the phone's voice recognition). Improve text: rewrites what you typed or dictated in clear, technical language. A window shows the before and after; tap Use this text to keep it.

Anything that got in the way of the day: tap the type (Material / delivery, Rain, Equipment, Safety / accident, Crew / absences, Visit / inspection, Design / conflict, Other) and describe what happened and the impact. Why it matters This is the section that protects the contractor in a delay claim: rain that stopped the pour, a late delivery, an inspection that did not show up — recorded on the day it happened. Issues & delays

Take photo opens the camera; From gallery picks existing photos. Each photo gets a stamp inside the image with the job, date, time and GPS coordinates, and is reduced on the phone (for example, 4.2 MB becomes about 300 KB) so it uploads fast even on a weak signal. Add a caption to each photo (for example, rebar before the pour). If the phone has no GPS, the job's location is used, and the stamp says so. Photos: camera or gallery

The bar at the bottom says what is still missing — for example, Missing: at least one person in manpower, at least one activity described — or that the report is ready. Then tap Submit for approval. The bottom bar: what is missing and Submit for approval A report needs, at least: the weather of the morning and of the afternoon, one person in the crew and one activity described. Without photos, KORbuild asks before submitting: Submitting without photos asks for confirmation Everything you type is saved on the phone as you go, even without signal. You can leave the report and come back later.

What it is for: most days look like the day before. Copying saves typing. On the job screen, tap or copy from a previous report. Choose the report to copy from (the most recent comes selected) and tap Copy. Choose which report to copy The new report brings the crew (with absences reset to zero), the equipment and the activities still in progress. Weather, photos and issues are not copied: they belong to the day.

What it is for: a workday without work on the job (rain, holiday, job on hold) still needs a record — it justifies the day and stops the reminders. On the job screen, tap No work today. Choose the reason: Rain / unworkable weather, Holiday or day off, Job put on hold by the client, Material shortage, Strike or work stoppage or Other reason, and add a note if you want. Tap Log it. The day is recorded as that day's report, it goes to the office and the reminders for that day stop.

If a past workday has no report, it appears in the red late report box on Today (up to the last 3 workdays). Tap it and fill out the report as usual — you can also copy from a previous one. A report submitted after the deadline is accepted, but it is marked Submitted late in the report and in the PDF, with the date and time of the first submission and the deadline it missed.

titulo: Fix a report the office sent back
texto: On Today, the red box The office requested changes to report #… shows the job, the date and the reason, in quotes. Tap Fix now →. The report opens with the request at the top. Make the changes and tap Resubmit. A request for changes on the foreman's Today screen A resubmission after a request for changes does not count as late: what counts is the first submission.

Nothing special to do: KORbuild works offline. While you fill out the report, everything is saved on the phone. If you submit without signal, the report is Saved on this device and waits in a queue. As soon as the connection comes back, it uploads by itself, photo by photo, and the office receives it. After the first visit, the whole app opens without internet. The indicator at the top of the screen (Online) shows the connection. In the prototype Tap Online to simulate losing the signal, and tap again to come back online.
History lists every report you filled out, newest first, with its status (Draft, Awaiting approval, Changes requested, Approved). Tap one to open it. History on the phone

titulo: Office: follow the jobs on the Dashboard
texto: What it is for: seeing, at a glance, which jobs reported today and what is waiting for you. General contractor or subcontractor The office screens are the same for both, but a general contractor sees every subcontractor on its jobs: one status light per subcontractor on each job, and the reports of all of them in the queue. A subcontractor sees its own reports; the ones on a general contractor's job wait for the general contractor to approve. Who can do it Anyone with View all jobs (default roles: Admin and Project manager). The Dashboard shows: The numbers of the day: today's reports received

titulo: Office: review and approve a report
texto: Who can do it Anyone with Approve reports and send to the client (default roles: Admin and Project manager) — at the general contractor of the job, or at the subcontractor when the job is directly with the owner. Open Approvals (or Review on the Dashboard). Approvals: the queue of reports The report opens exactly as the client will see it: job, client, prepared by, current phase, deadline, weather, manpower, equipment, work performed, issues, photos. On the right, the Review panel and the report's History (who started it, submitted it, when it arrived). Reviewing a report Choose: Approve and s

titulo: Office: request changes from the field
texto: On the report, click Request changes from the field. In What needs to be fixed?, write the reason (for example, missing the photo of the rebar before the pour). Click Send request. Requesting changes The report goes back to the field with the reason, and appears in red on the foreman's Today screen. When the foreman resubmits, the report comes back to your queue.

titulo: Office: share the report with the client
texto: On an approved report: Copy link for the client — copies a link you can send by email or message. The client opens it in any browser, without an account. View as the client — opens that link, so you can see what the client sees. Download PDF — the report as a PDF, with the company logo, the job, the weather, the tables, the photos with captions, date and GPS, the seal and signatures. The client's page checks the seal every time it opens. If the content matches what was approved, it shows Authentic document, with who approved it and when. Each rule has an ID (DLY-nnn) so it can be quoted in meetings, tests and change requests. The Status column says whether the rule works in the prototype today. Source These rules come from the prototype's code and from the product decisions recorded in the project documentation (daily report alerts, jobs, schedule). Where something was not decided yet, it is marked To be confirmed.

ID Rule Status DLY-001 Every job has one person responsible for its daily report. Reminders and alerts go to that person. Working DLY-002 A report is required for each workday of the job's calendar (default: Monday to Saturday). Days that are not workdays generate no alert; if there is work, a report can still be filled out. Working DLY-003 Only jobs in progress require reports. Jobs on hold or completed do not appear in the field and generate no alert. A job also requires nothing before its start date. Working DLY-004 The daily deadline is 6 PM of the day itself. Working DLY-005 A day is done

ID Rule Status DLY-010 At 4 PM, the person responsible gets a reminder: today's report is missing. Working (app open) DLY-011 At 6 PM, the report of the day is late: the person responsible gets an alert. Working (app open) DLY-012 At 8 AM of the next day, the office sees on the Dashboard and in notifications every job with no report on its last workday, with the person responsible. Working DLY-013 Alerts go to the in-app notifications (bell) and to the phone's notifications. No SMS or email for now. Working DLY-022 Lateness is measured on the first submission: resubmitting after a request for changes does not count as late. Working

Crew is the crew time clock. It records who worked, where, on which cost code and for how long, turns that into weekly timesheets approved for payroll, and into labor cost per job: budget × actual × forecast to completion.

Who worked, where and how much? Punches with GPS, the job's geofence and an optional crew photo. How much do I pay? The weekly timesheet, with overtime calculated by the company's work rule, approved and exported to payroll as a CSV file. How much is this job costing, and will it finish within budget? Labor cost by job and cost code, with the forecast to completion — early enough to act. The same punches fill the crew of the Daily report, so the field enters the crew once.

Foreman Phone Crew time clock: clocks in the whole crew from one phone; Hours: the crew's week with alerts. Employees, hourly rates, labor burden and work rules are set up in Settings, because every module uses them. Crew only reads them.

Term Meaning Punch One time clock record: clock in, break start, break end, switch job, arrived, clock out. A punch is never edited or deleted; a correction is a new punch, marked as an edit, with who and why. Geofence A circle around the job (150 m by default, set per job). A punch outside it is accepted but flagged for the office to review. Cost code The service the hour was spent on (foundation, structure, masonry…). Every hour belongs to a job and a cost code. Travel Moving from one job to another during the workday. It is paid time. Timesheet One person's week, Monday to Sunday: total, re

Daily: the report's crew can be filled from who clocked in on the job that day. Jobs (Settings › Jobs): the job's location and geofence radius come from the job setup. Only jobs in progress appear in the time clock. Settings: employees and hourly rates (with effective dates), labor burden, work rules (overtime and breaks).

This manual walks through Crew one task at a time: first the worker and the foreman (on the phone), then the office (on the computer). Screen names, buttons and messages are written exactly as they appear in KORbuild, in bold. Before you start Crew opens in the area of your role: a worker goes straight to My time clock (no modules screen); a foreman opens on the Crew time clock; the office opens on Now. If you do not see a screen described here, your role does not include it — see Roles and permissions.

titulo: Worker: clock in and out on your own phone
texto: What it is for: recording your own day, with the time and the location of each punch. Who can do it Anyone with Clock in and out (self) (default role: Worker). Open KORbuild. My time clock opens directly, with the Official clock time, today's status (for example, Not clocked in yet) and one big button with what fits now. Tap Clock in. A window opens: Job — where you are working (only jobs in progress are listed). The distance to the job, in green when you are inside the geofence ✓, or in red when you are outside it. Cost code — the service you are working on. Crew photo (optional) — opens the

titulo: Foreman: clock in the whole crew
texto: What it is for: one phone clocks in the whole crew at once — the most common way crews work on site. Who can do it Anyone with Clock in the crew (default role: Foreman). Open Crew. The Crew time clock shows the Official clock time, how many are working, on break, traveling and off site, and the list of the crew with each person's status. Select people: tap each one, or Select all. The bar at the bottom says how many are selected and turns on the buttons that make sense for them (for example, Clock in (6)). Tap Clock in. KORbuild locates the phone and shows the distance to the job ("inside the
Break and Back from break cover the meal break (one tap, no window). Clock out ends the day. KORbuild asks Clock out now? — if someone keeps working, leave them out of the selection.

Select the people and tap Switch job. Choose Which job? and tap Leave for the job. The punch is made where you are (the job you are leaving), and the travel starts. Travel time to the other job counts as hours worked. When you get there, tap Arrived, choose the cost code on this job and Record arrival. The arrival is checked against the geofence of the new job. Switch job: the travel to the other job is paid time

Hours shows the crew's week: hours per person and per day. A red ! means something to check — a missing clock-out, an off-site punch or a missed break. The office approves the hours. Crew hours, with the alerts

titulo: Office: see who is working now
texto: Who can do it Anyone with View time clock and timesheets (default roles: Admin and Project manager). Now shows: Working now, On break, Traveling and Hours today. Off-site punches to review: punches outside the geofence, with the distance from the job. View day opens the person's day map; Reviewed marks it as checked (the punch stays recorded as outside the geofence). Each job with the people clocked in on it, since when and on which cost code. Now

Who can do it Anyone with Approve and edit timesheets (default roles: Admin and Project manager). Open Timesheets. Use Previous and Next to change the week (Monday to Sunday). At the top: Hours this week, Overtime hours, Labor cost (with the cost permission) and Awaiting approval. The table has one row per person: hours per day, Total, OT (overtime), Cost and Status (Approved, Awaiting approval…). Check the people to approve and click Approve selected, or open a person and click Approve week. Click a person to see their Employee week: total, regular, overtime and cost, and each day with its segments (work on a job and cost code, break, travel), the Day map and Edit. One person's week, awaiting approval
Return sends the week back to the foreman. Write What needs to be reviewed? (for example, confirm Tuesday's clock-out with the foreman) and click Return. Returning a timesheet with the reason

titulo: Edit a day (for example, a forgotten clock-out)
texto: On the person's week, click Edit on the day. Choose the Punch (clock out, break start, break end, clock in), the Time and the Reason (for example, forgot to clock out; confirmed with the foreman). Click Save edit. The edit is added as a new punch, marked as an edit, with your name and the reason. The original punches stay visible. Editing a day: a new punch with time and reason

Export CSV (approved) downloads the approved hours of the week, one line per segment (week, employee, trade, date, job, cost code, type, start, end, hours, status), ready for payroll systems such as QuickBooks, Gusto or ADP.

titulo: Office: see a person's day on the map
texto: Day map (from Now › View day, or from a person's week) shows the day on a street map: Clock in (green E) and Clock out (dark S), the number of entries and the distance traveled; the jobs, numbered in the order visited, with the geofence; the location points recorded during the workday, connected with arrows in the direction of travel; off-site punches in red; Play back replays the day, with the clock on screen; Full screen enlarges the map. Each rule has an ID (CRW-nnn) so it can be quoted in meetings, tests and change requests. The Status column says whether the rule works in the prototype today. Source These rules come from the prototype's code and from the Crew specification recorded in the project documentation. Open points are marked To be confirmed at the end.

ID Rule Status CRW-001 A punch is never edited or deleted. A correction is a new punch, marked as an edit, with who made it, when and the reason. The original stays visible. Working CRW-002 Every hour belongs to a job and a cost code. That is what makes cost by job possible. Working CRW-003 No rounding. Every minute is paid; the "7-minute rule" is not used. Working CRW-004 The foreman can punch several people at once. Each punch records who registered it. Working CRW-005 Each punch records the time, the job, the cost code, the GPS position and its accuracy, whether it was inside the geofence,

ID Rule Status CRW-010 Each job has a geofence: its location and a radius (150 m by default, 50 to 2,000 m, set in the job setup). Working CRW-011 The geofence flags, it does not block. A punch outside it is accepted, marked off site, and goes to the office to review. GPS is often inaccurate inside concrete structures. Working CRW-012 Without GPS on the phone, the job's location is used. Working

ID Rule Status CRW-020 Travel between jobs during the workday is paid time (29 CFR 785.38). The commute from home to the job is not. Working CRW-021 On a switch job, the punch is made where the person is (the job being left) and travel starts; Arrived is checked against the geofence of the new job. Working CRW-022 Breaks are not paid. The minimum and after how many hours come from the work rule (New Hampshire default: 30 min after 5 hours, RSA 275:30-a). A missed break raises an alert. Working CRW-023 Missing clock-out: a past day left open counts no hours until someone edits it. It raises an

ID Rule Status CRW-030 Overtime follows the work rule in effect (Settings). Company default: New Hampshire / federal FLSA — over 40 hours in the week (Monday to Sunday) pays 1.5×. Working CRW-031 If the work rule has daily overtime (for example, over 8 h → 1.5×; over 12 h → 2×), hours already paid as daily overtime do not count again toward weekly overtime. Working CRW-032 A work rule applies to whole weeks, starting on a Monday. Working CRW-033 Weighted regular rate: if the hourly rate changed during the week, the overtime premium (0.5×) is calculated on the week's weighted average. Working C

ID Rule Status CRW-040 Hourly rate with effective date: a change creates a new rate "from" a date, with a reason. The past is never rewritten: each day uses the rate in effect that day. Working CRW-041 A new hourly rate cannot start inside a week that is already approved (it went to payroll). Working CRW-042 Job cost = hours × rate in effect that day + the overtime premium split across jobs by that week's hours + labor burden on payroll. Working CRW-043 Labor burden has effective dates (Settings › Labor burden). Default: 32.05% (FICA 7.65%, FUTA 0.60%, SUTA 2.80%, workers' comp 14.00%, benefit

ID Rule Status CRW-050 Location only while clocked in. Recorded at each punch, when the app is opened during the workday and every 15 minutes on site (every 5 while traveling). Never during breaks, while clocked out or off hours. The worker is told so. Simulated (see Prototype status) CRW-051 The day map is seen by those who follow the time clock (office). Working

ID Rule Status CRW-060 Dollar amounts (costs, wages on timesheets) require See costs and dollar amounts. Workers and foremen see hours, never money. Working CRW-061 Approve, return, edit and export require Approve and edit timesheets. Without it, timesheets are read-only. Working CRW-062 Each company clocks in its own employees. A subcontractor never sees another company's people. On a general contractor's job, the general contractor sees the subcontractor's people on site — names, trade, time in, hours — but never wages, labor burden or cost.
